content: This medication, cidofovir, is used in combination with probenecid to treat a specific viral eye infection known as cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis in individuals with AIDS. It helps reduce the risk of blindness and other vision-related complications. Cidofovir belongs to a class of drugs called antivirals. Administration and Dosage: Cidofovir is administered as an intravenous (IV) injection, typically every 1 to 2 weeks, as directed by your doctor. The medication is infused slowly over one hour and should never be injected directly into the eyes. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition, body weight, and response to treatment. Before each dose, you will usually receive IV fluids to help protect your kidneys. Additionally, your doctor will instruct you to take probenecid orally before and after receiving cidofovir. It is essential to drink plenty of fluids during treatment unless otherwise directed by your doctor. Before use, inspect the medication for particles or discoloration; do not use it if either is present. Precautions: Cidofovir can cause serious, potentially fatal kidney damage. To minimize this risk, your doctor will prescribe probenecid and IV fluids. Avoid using other medications that may harm the kidneys, such as amphotericin B, foscarnet, pentamidine, vancomycin, aminoglycosides (e.g., tobramycin), or NSAIDs (e.g., ibuprofen, naproxen) within seven days before and during treatment. Kidney function and blood tests will be performed before each dose to monitor for side effects. This medication may also suppress your immune system, reducing your ability to fight infections. Cidofovir has been shown to cause tumors in laboratory animals, and while there is no direct evidence in humans, it is considered potentially carcinogenic. Side Effects: Common side effects include nausea, vomiting, and headache, particularly due to probenecid. Taking probenecid with food may help reduce these symptoms. Serious allergic reactions to cidofovir are rare but possible. If you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling, severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing, seek medical attention immediately. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of severe side effects. Keep a list of all prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products you use, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Avoid medications that may harm your kidneys, as mentioned earlier. Always check the labels of over-the-counter medications for NSAIDs, as they may be present in products like ibuprofen or naproxen. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Cidofovir should only be used during pregnancy if absolutely necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. The manufacturer recommends avoiding pregnancy during treatment. Men with female partners should use effective barrier protection (e.g., latex or polyurethane condoms) during treatment and for at least 90 days after stopping the medication. It is unknown if cidofovir passes into breast milk, but if you have HIV, breastfeeding is not recommended as it may transmit the virus to your baby. Missed Dose: It is crucial to adhere to the prescribed dosing schedule. If you miss a dose of cidofovir, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for a missed one. If you miss a dose of probenecid, inform your doctor or pharmacist right away. Storage and Disposal: Consult the product instructions or your pharmacist for proper storage details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. For less severe cases, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Notes: Regular medical and laboratory tests, such as kidney function and eye exams, are necessary while using this medication. Keep all medical appointments. To reduce the risk of spreading HIV to others, use effective barrier methods (e.g., latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams) during sexual activity. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information tailored to your specific health needs.
